newsitem.title: USA: Rubin says still need US balanced budget agreement.
newsitem.headline: Rubin says still need US balanced budget agreement.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said Wednesday there was still a need to push ahead with implementing the balanced budget agreement despite a reduction in the U.S. deficit.
Wall Street analysts expect the deficit to be reduced to $50 billion by the end of the current fiscal year which ends Sept 30 from the $107 billion deficit posted in fiscal 1996.
"I still think it's very important we go ahead with this balanced budget agreement," Rubin said to reporters after meeting with House Democrats.
"We are getting the benefits right now of very good times and you would expect that to swell our coffers in terms of tax revenue," Rubin said.

However for long-term structural fiscal responsility, it was important to move ahead with the five-year balanced budget agreement reached by congressional leaders and the White House in May, Rubin said.

The agreement has more savings than combined tax cuts and spending increases, Rubin said, "so over time the balanced budget agreement will put the country in better fiscal shape than what would occur without the balanced budget agreement."
Rubin, asked about Japan, said Japan's prime minister has on several occasions stated that that country's objective is domestic demand-led growth and the avoidance of sustained external surpluses.
"I have no reason to think that they will not continue to work toward the objectives they themselves have stated," Rubin said.
